perspective:
**Bradley Ochoa’s available information / subjective reconstruction**

- I am Bradley Ochoa, a Hispanic man and a salesperson at a marketing firm. I have a high-school education and tend to favor proven, traditional sales methods. Katherine Lasiloo is my colleague and the marketing manager.
- In our meeting-room discussion, I had prepared data and charts from our last five campaigns to argue for traditional sales techniques. I told Katherine I appreciated her digital strategies but believed core sales would benefit more from traditional methods. She said the market is evolving and asked how I reconcile my data with increasing online engagement. I replied that I don’t want to abandon digital marketing, but I’m frustrated that proven methods are being sidelined without proper consideration. She said she understood my frustration, that it’s about balance, and suggested analyzing the data together to integrate both approaches.
- After the meeting, Katherine shared recent digital campaign success stories that significantly boosted engagement and sales. I felt uncertain and asked how those strategies are developed. She said it’s about targeting the right audience with the right message and offered to walk me through the analytics and decision-making. I admitted I had doubts about moving away from traditional methods, but seeing the outcomes made me want to understand more. She said she was glad I was open and suggested diving deeper into the data.
- I became hopeful and proposed a joint strategy meeting to combine traditional and digital marketing. Katherine agreed, saying combining our strengths could lead to better results and suggesting we schedule a time to brainstorm and outline next steps. I said I was hopeful and appreciated her willingness to collaborate. She said she looked forward to leveraging each other’s strengths.
- After the joint meeting, I was excited and worked overtime to prepare a board presentation draft integrating both our ideas. I told Katherine about it. She reviewed it, called it comprehensive and well thought out, and said my hard work showed. I thanked her, said I was convinced the integrated approach would set us apart from competitors, and that I wanted to nail the presentation. She was confident and suggested going through it once more to fine-tune.
- After the presentation and our work on the project, I thanked Katherine, saying I learned a lot and was grateful for my growth through our collaboration. She said it was a pleasure and that my openness made it a successful partnership. I proposed regular strategy sessions to keep momentum. She agreed, saying regular sessions would keep us on top of our game and market trends.

**Not available to Bradley:** Katherine’s private thoughts, her INTP personality, her bachelor’s degree, and her American Indian identity unless he was told or directly observed it; hidden events or narrator-only information.
